b2-81.title: A day at the office
b2-81.story: Anna has a summer internship at a small company in Kyiv. On Monday morning, the printer ran out of [[toner]] just before an important meeting. Then everyone heard that the [[big boss]] was visiting the office that afternoon. Anna was trying to finish a presentation, answer emails and order lunch at the same time, but [[multitasking]] only made her slower. Max, who works there as an [[IT specialist]], fixed the printer in five minutes. Meanwhile, the [[web designer]] was redrawing the new homepage, and the [[web developer]] was building it with a simple [[drag-and-drop]] editor. The [[webmaster]] noticed that half of the text on the site was [[copy-paste]] from an old brochure, so Anna rewrote it quickly. At the meeting, the boss spoke for an hour about budgets, targets and other [[blah-blah]]. But at the end, she praised the team's new website, and Anna smiled all the way home.

b2-82.title: Working in media
b2-82.story: Max's sister Sofia works at a small agency that creates [[media content]] for local businesses. This month she is leading a [[media project]] about young people in Kyiv. The client wanted more [[video content]], so the team planned a [[photoshoot]] and a series of short films. A [[photojournalist]] friend agreed to take pictures by the river and on the busy streets. For the website, Sofia recorded a [[video interview]] with Anna about student life. She also wanted to try [[podcasting]], so she turned their chat into the first episode of a podcast. Because some guests lived in other cities, the panel discussion was held in an [[online format]]. Before anything went public, a [[media expert]] did a careful [[fact-check]] of every number. She found one mistake, and Sofia fixed it just in time. When the project launched on Friday, the client called to say it was their best campaign yet.

b2-83.title: Friday night at the pub
b2-83.story: On Friday, Anna's dad took the family to a cozy pub near their house to celebrate his birthday. They arrived during [[happy hour]], so the place was busy and loud. Dad ordered a pint of local [[ale]], and his old friend chose a cold [[lager]]. Anna and Taras had warm apple [[cider]], which tasted like autumn. In the back room, Taras tried [[darts]] for the first time and hit the board only once. Grandpa, meanwhile, beat everyone at [[snooker]] and looked very proud of himself. Anna loved the [[vibe]]: old photos on the walls, quiet music and lots of laughter. Then Mama brought out a birthday cake she had secretly made that morning. She had whipped the cream with her new electric [[mixer]] and added a little coffee [[liqueur]] to it. Dad said it was the best part of the evening.

b2-84.title: At the hotel bar
b2-84.story: For their fiftieth anniversary, Anna's grandparents invited the whole family to a hotel in Lviv. In the evening, everyone met at the hotel bar, where a friendly [[bartender]] was polishing glasses. Grandpa, as always, asked for a small [[cognac]], and Grandma chose a classic [[martini]] with an olive. Dad couldn't choose between [[whiskey]] and [[bourbon]], so the bartender patiently explained the difference. Mama ordered a [[margarita]], while her cousin had a [[gin]] with lime. A man at the next table asked for [[tequila]], but the bar had just run out. Anna, who doesn't drink alcohol, asked for a [[tonic]] with lemon and ice. Then the bartender made Taras a special alcohol-free [[cocktail]] with mint and berries and called it "The Lviv Sunset." Taras was delighted, and Grandpa raised his glass to fifty wonderful years.

b2-85.title: A costume party
b2-85.story: Lisa got an [[invite]] to Ira's costume party and immediately texted Anna. The party was in a big old house, and Ira's aunt, a professional event [[coordinator]], had organized everything. Anna came as a [[pirate]], with a paper hat and a fake parrot on her shoulder. Max arrived as a [[zombie]], and his makeup was so realistic that Lisa screamed when she saw him. Ira's cousin from Scotland wore a real [[kilt]], which everyone thought was a costume. The [[catering]] was excellent: tiny pizzas, fresh fruit and a chocolate fountain. In the garden, there was even a small [[carousel]] for the younger kids. Later, everyone sang [[karaoke]], and Max's zombie version of a love song won first prize. At midnight, Ira threw [[confetti]] over the dance floor. Three days later, Anna was still finding [[glitter]] from Lisa's costume in her hair.

b2-86.title: The town festival
b2-86.story: Every summer, the small town where Anna's grandparents live holds a music [[fest]] by the river. This year it began with a colorful [[carnival]], with dancers and giant puppets parading down the main street. Later, a group of Mexican students turned the town square into a real [[fiesta]], with bright flags and loud trumpets. Taras was hungry all day, so the family kept going back to the [[snack bar]] for corn and hot dogs. In the evening, Anna and Max watched a [[stand-up]] show by a young local comedian, and Grandpa laughed louder than anyone. At the end, the organizers held a [[giveaway]], and Taras won a bicycle with his lucky ticket. He rode it home proudly, ringing the bell all the way.

b2-87.title: Our band's first gig
b2-87.story: Max and his friends have a small rock band, and last Saturday they played their first gig. Lisa is the band's [[vocalist]], and Max plays guitar and is the main [[songwriter]]. When the local club posted the [[lineup]] for the night, they were amazed to see their name right before a well-known group. Ira jokingly called herself their [[tour manager]], although the "tour" was just one bus ride across Kyiv. To everyone's surprise, the show was [[sold out]] by Friday. Backstage, Max was so nervous that he forgot the [[intro]] to their first song during the sound check. Then the [[MC]] announced their name, and the crowd started clapping. Somehow Max's fingers found the right notes, and Lisa's voice filled the room. It wasn't a perfect [[live show]], but nobody cared, and Anna cheered the loudest.

b2-88.title: In the record shop
b2-88.story: On Saturday, Anna went with her dad to a small record shop in the center of Kyiv. Dad went straight to the [[funk]] section and started telling her about the music of his youth. Anna found an old [[blues]] album and decided to buy it for Grandpa. The owner, a cheerful man with a gray beard, said this album was recorded in [[stereo]] and sounded much better on [[vinyl]] than online. He also mentioned that a local band was celebrating the [[release]] of their first album in the shop that evening. Anna and Dad stayed for the concert and bought some [[merch]], a T-shirt with the band's logo. On Sunday, Grandpa played the record three times and danced with Grandma in the kitchen.
